_note: Month-specific copy. Strings are Jinja templates rendered against the market data file, so numbers are pulled from data rather than typed. Review every sentence when the data changes — the judgments (e.g. 'seller-leaning') are not automatic. September 2026 changes from August: condo closings turned POSITIVE (-22.8% to +13.9%) and condo days to contract ROSE (80 to 89), so the August 'fewer closings' framing and every 'contract time fell' sentence on the condo side were rewritten. Condo supply tightened to 5.1 months, so that verdict moved from 'close to balanced' toward sellers.
glanceLede: Supply is down from a year ago in both property types, sharply so. Here are the four key measures for each, side by side.

insights.lede: What the {{ dataMonth }} figures point to, tied directly to the tables on page 3.

cards.title: There is less to choose from than a year ago.
cards.body: Active single-family listings fell to {{ s.sfh.m.inventory.current | int }} from {{ s.sfh.m.inventory.prior | int }}, and condo/townhome listings fell {{ s.condo.m.inventory.pct | abspct }} to {{ s.condo.m.inventory.current | int }}. Both property types have fewer homes on the market than in {{ priorMonth }}.

cards.title: Single-family homes went under contract quickly.
cards.body: The median fell from {{ s.sfh.m.daysToContract.prior }} days to {{ s.sfh.m.daysToContract.current }}, a drop of {{ s.sfh.m.daysToContract.pct | abspct }}. With supply at {{ s.sfh.m.monthsSupply.current | dec1 }} months, down from {{ s.sfh.m.monthsSupply.prior | dec1 }}, and sales closing at {{ s.sfh.m.olpReceived.current | dec1 }}% of original list price, the single-family side leans to sellers.

cards.title: Condo supply tightened considerably.
cards.body: Supply dropped from {{ s.condo.m.monthsSupply.prior | dec1 }} to {{ s.condo.m.monthsSupply.current | dec1 }} months, the largest move in either property type, on {{ s.condo.m.inventory.pct | abspct }} fewer active listings. Closings rose {{ s.condo.m.closedSales.pct | abspct }} to {{ s.condo.m.closedSales.current | int }} and sales closed at {{ s.condo.m.olpReceived.current | dec1 }}% of original list price, up from {{ s.condo.m.olpReceived.prior | dec1 }}%.

cards.title: Condos still took longer to go under contract.
cards.body: The median rose from {{ s.condo.m.daysToContract.prior }} days to {{ s.condo.m.daysToContract.current }}, so even with supply tightening, a condo or townhome listing should be planned around a longer marketing period than a house.

cards.title: Read the {{ s.condo.m.medianPrice.pct | signed }} condo median with care.
cards.body: The median was {{ s.condo.m.medianPrice.current | usd }} against {{ s.condo.m.medianPrice.prior | usd }} a year earlier, on {{ s.condo.m.closedSales.current | int }} closings. At that volume the mix of which buildings and price points traded moves the median more than any change in what units are worth.

cards.title: Cash buyers remain a large part of the market.

insights.localLine: County figures blend distinct local markets, including Stuart, Palm City, Jensen Beach, Hobe Sound and Port Salerno, and conditions in any one of them can differ from the county median.

ctaLede: County medians are a starting point. We'll look at recent sales and active competition where you own or want to buy, and build a plan around your property type and timeline, with no obligation.
disclaimer: This report summarizes past market activity in Martin County for the months shown. It is not an appraisal, a prediction of future prices, or investment advice, and county medians do not reflect the value of any specific property. Cash shares were calculated by DO Homes Group from the reported counts. Information is believed reliable but not guaranteed. Not intended to solicit properties currently listed with another broker.
